svg.title: Email Coverage by Enrichment Setup
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-email-coverage-by-enrichment-setup; chapter number: 4; title: Email Coverage by Enrichment Setup; subtitle: Single databases versus stacked Clay waterfalls; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 40% to 90% of a list with a usable email, depending on setup; buckets: label: Apollo 'Valid' Emails That Verify; low: 40; high: 40; notes: AJ Cassata sees only 40% of Apollo 'valids' verify on 5,000 leads. Mailing invalids burns inboxes and domains.; label: Traditional Single Database; low: 40; high: 50; notes: Coverage from one traditional database, per AJ Cassata.; label: Stacked Clay Waterfall; low: 60; high: 80; notes: Cheapest-first waterfall capped around four steps. Cassata deletes any provider charging over 10 credits per row.; label: 11-Provider Waterfall with Validation; low: 90; high: 90; notes: Matt Lucero finds 9 of 10 valid emails with Prospeo and LeadMagic moved to the front and validation between steps.; caption: Stacking providers roughly doubles coverage over a single database, while depth of the waterfall remains a live disagreement.; assumptions note: Percentages measure different things (verification rate, coverage, hit rate) across different lists. Romain Osman skips the waterfall for Prospeo alone.; note: Sources - AJ Cassata (6l8CThrSJEY @ 00:03:00, 12s-u4y1VF0 @ 00:04:38), Matt Lucero (jEkDgA8hPmo @ 00:25:01).
